title: Overt-gaze steady-state visual target decoding
scientific_question: Can a frozen method identify the instructed overt-gaze flicker target from a four-second EEG epoch for an entirely held-out person, beyond constant and frequency-mapping controls?
primary_outputs: One of four source labels ordered1up,2left,3right,4down; corresponding nominal reference frequencies60/[5,7,9,11]Hz.

primary.rationale: Measures complete held-person protocol-label accuracy without treating phase/trial replication as independent humans; raw CCA scores are not calibrated probabilities.

comparators.name: Unfitted two-harmonic CCA
comparators.inputs: Same ten-channel400 sample epoch and nominal frequencies60/[5,7,9,11]Hz; no training labels.
comparators.procedure: Pinned reference centers/scales and computes rank-aware orthonormal spans, then maximal canonical correlation to sine/cosine first/second harmonic columns. Constant/rank-zero epochs yield zero scores. Implemented but not run on authentic EEG.

comparators.name: Constant-score context baseline
comparators.inputs: No per-trial labels/cue/timing; four zero scores.
comparators.procedure: Use reference --mode constant; earliest-class ties retained. The public representation exposes no useful trial timing metadata.

comparators.name: Frequency-column permutation diagnostic
comparators.procedure: Rotate four CCA score columns left by one; keep original labels/IDs. A diagnostic for frequency mapping, not a neural-mechanism or randomization p-value.
